$about: THE source of colour for both the app and the website. Nothing here is
typed twice anywhere else: Tools/GenerateTokens.swift writes
App/Vocula/UI/ThemeTokens.swift, Icon/*.svg and build/tokens.css from it,
and `--check` fails if any of those drifted. Edit this file, run the tool.
Values are OKLCH wherever the colour belongs to the brand, because that is
the space the palette was designed in: one hue, one chroma, lightness
carrying the light/dark split. HEX is allowed for greys that were never
derived from the accent. The tool converts OKLCH to sRGB ONCE and hands
the same HEX to Swift, CSS and SVG — a value converted twice can clip
twice and differently, which is how #8A4C00 would have ended up two
colours.
`scope` is not decoration. `both` means the app and the site must agree.
`app` and `web` mean the token is deliberately platform-only, and a
reviewer who finds it missing on the other side has found the design, not
a bug.
`use` is a WHITELIST, and only the mark carries one. The mark's colour is
deliberately exaggerated, and it is not a palette colour: a 16-point icon
is a tiny object fighting for attention among other people's icons, and
the interface colours — correct at the size of a sidebar row — go grey and
dull down there. So the exaggeration is licensed for exactly two surfaces
and forbidden everywhere else. An interface element painted mark.hot is a
bug, and so is an icon painted accent.fill.

tokens.name: accent.fill
tokens.note: Brass as a FILL: a sidebar selection, a tinted control, a chip, the site's button.

tokens.name: accent.ink
tokens.note: Brass as TEXT. On light it must be dark to be read at all; on dark the fill already reads, so the two are one value. Light leaves sRGB and is clipped — deliberately, once, here.

tokens.name: accent.on
tokens.note: What is written ON the fill. Needed because brass is LIGHT: white on it is 2.04, unreadable. Anything painting white on the accent is a bug.

tokens.name: mark.hot
tokens.note: The MARK's orange — app icon and the indicator's ramp, nothing else. Hotter than accent.fill ON PURPOSE: both surfaces are drawn OUTSIDE our windows, among other people's icons and over other people's documents, where the mark competes for attention rather than sitting in an interface. Leaves sRGB, clipped to the gamut edge. Not drift. Do not 'correct' it to accent.fill.

tokens.name: mark.cool
tokens.note: The cool end of the mark's ramp, in the icon and in the indicator WHILE A SESSION RUNS. Not the resting line — see pane.resting.

tokens.name: pane.resting
tokens.note: The indicator's line when nothing is being said. Stays neutral on purpose: the line sits above the Dock all day over other people's windows, and colour belongs to the time the microphone is open.

tokens.name: warning.text
tokens.note: Hue 45, not the 60-65 it used to be: at 65 it was 5.4 degrees from brass and 'needs attention' read as 'selected'. At 45 the gap is 25 degrees in both appearances.

tokens.name: warning.backing
tokens.note: Light only. On dark the backing is warning.text at 8% — an alpha, not a colour, so it lives in Swift.

tokens.name: warning.border
tokens.note: Light only, same reason as warning.backing.

tokens.name: window.bg
tokens.note: Behind the detail column. Not derived from the accent, hence HEX.

tokens.name: text.secondary
tokens.note: Warm on light, cool on dark. The asymmetry is deliberate: a warm grey on warm white reads as paper, the same grey on near-black reads as dirt.

tokens.name: site.bg
tokens.note: The site's neutrals carry a trace of the accent's hue; the app's do not. Two different rooms, and they are allowed to be.

$note: The five bars of the 32pt icon are the continuous ramp sampled at each
bar's REAL centre — the bars sit on an even grid, so these are not
quarters. Interpolated in OKLab rather than sRGB, or the middle steps go
muddy. The generator computes them; they are never typed into the SVG.
